bullets.title: NVDA/AVGO: Management firmly dismisses AI slowdown; Citi sets NVDA PT $315, AVGO PT $515
bullets.body: Both Jensen Huang (NVDA) and Hock Tan (AVGO) aggressively pushed back on AI spending slowdown fears at the Communacopia/TMT conference circuit, with Broadcom reaffirming its $115B FY2027 AI semiconductor revenue target. Citi maintains Buy on both with PTs of $315 (~21x C27E EPS) and $515 (~19x F28 EPS) respectively, arguing U.S.-China tech competition makes a meaningful AI investment pullback unlikely. NVDA's Rubin platform shows 7x better token throughput per megawatt vs. Blackwell per GS analysis, potentially generating 2x+ more profit per gigawatt.

bullets.title: AI safety/semis rotation: SOX -5.9% Monday; software vs. semis pair hit 2.4-sigma; semis stabilizing Tuesday
bullets.body: Dario Amodei's AI pacing essay triggered the largest-ever Software>Semis 1-day move (+12.5%, 2.4 sigma) on Monday; SOX fell ~5.9% while IGV gained. JPM and others note the rotation into inference/hyperscaler plays (GOOGL, META, MSFT) and out of training-leveraged names (CIEN). Semis are rebounding Tuesday (INTC +1.8%, NVDA/AVGO +75bps) as management pushback takes hold and investors view the safety debate as unlikely to alter capex trajectories.

bullets.title: JPM upgrades META to Overweight; names AMZN, GOOGL, SPOT as top Internet picks
bullets.body: JPM's Fall 2026 Internet sector update upgrades META to Overweight with focus on AI models and agents, citing AI monetization traction and hyperscaler capex durability. Top large-cap picks are AMZN, GOOGL, and SPOT; SHOP and TTWO are top SMID-cap picks. US Cloud sales up 50% y/y with backlogs >100% of sales; only 8% of enterprises have deployed AI agents at scale, suggesting significant runway.

bullets.title: AMD: Pre-quiet period check bullish — datacenter to >2x CY27, Helios ramp on track; Wolfe OP $650 PT
bullets.body: Wolfe Research maintains Outperform on AMD at $650 PT following pre-quiet period call. Helios GPU ramp begins volume production in September with full quarter in 4Q; tight supply reflects allocation, not delay. Datacenter business expected to more than double in CY27 with CPU growing >70% y/y; gross margin dips ~100bps q/q in 4Q on Helios ramp but stabilizes ~55% in CY27. Bull case EPS $25+ implies 20x multiple.

bullets.title: PLTR: UBS reiterates Buy at 51x 2027 FCF; ACN set to benefit from Capgemini US govt divestiture
bullets.body: UBS remains a buyer of PLTR at 51x 2027 FCF multiple, arguing it is attractive relative to SNOW and CRWD given 90%+ growth. Separately, ACN is flagged as a beneficiary of Capgemini divesting its US Government business; UBS has a Street-high $275 PT on ACN. ACN was down 2.1% pre-market in broad software weakness.

bullets.title: ORCL: Third consecutive beat; raised FY27 guidance; layoffs beginning
bullets.body: Oracle delivered a third consecutive quarter of revenue and EPS upside in F1Q27 with accelerating top-line growth, per Mizuho. FY27 revenue and EPS guidance were raised; net cash capex expected at most $70B with FY27/28 as peak capex years. UBS separately notes ORCL is beginning a new round of layoffs. ORCL is flagged as a top pick by UBS alongside MSFT.

bullets.title: TEAM: ~7-10% cloud list price hike effective Dec 3; Mizuho bullish on 2-3 year DC-to-cloud migration runway
bullets.body: Atlassian implemented a high single-digit (~7-10%) cloud list price uplift and broad usage-based pricing expansion effective December 3, per Mizuho. Data center-to-cloud migrations provide a 2-3 year significant growth opportunity. TEAM was down 2.4% pre-market in broad SaaS weakness.

bullets.title: CRM: Unveils AIforce at Dreamforce — enterprise data layer for Claude, Slack, and third-party AI agents
bullets.body: Salesforce launched AIforce at Dreamforce, enabling access to Salesforce data, workflows, business logic, and permissions outside the native app via Claude, Slack (Slackforce), and other platforms. Initial releases include Claudeforce, Slackforce, and Agentforce Coworker. CRM was down ~2% pre-market in broad software selling.

bullets.title: ETSY: Multi-broker upgrade to Outperform — Oppenheimer $90 PT, Opco confirms GMS inflection
bullets.body: Oppenheimer upgraded ETSY to Outperform (from Perform) with a $90 PT (21% upside from $74.46), citing AI search improvements and non-app buyer traffic inflecting from -3% in Q2 to flat y/y in Q3. Opco corroborates: survey work shows reduced Google Search dependence; FY27/28 GMS growth raised to +5%. ETSY trades at 12x '27E EBITDA, a 10% discount to EBAY. Stock up ~3% pre-market.

bullets.title: NYT: Guggenheim upgrades to Buy, raises PT to $82 (17% upside)
bullets.body: Guggenheim's Curry Baker upgraded New York Times to Buy from Neutral and raised the price target to $82 from $70, implying ~17% upside from $70.34. The FactSet consensus PT is $77.62. NYT was up 1.4% pre-market ahead of the upgrade.

bullets.title: AKAM: Pre-quiet check — street mismodeling CIS growth (+41% vs realistic +37%); AI inference pipeline strong
bullets.body: TMT color from a sell-side pre-quiet period check flags street mismodeling AKAM Q3 CIS at +41% y/y vs a more realistic +37%; GPU shipment timing is the primary risk to 50%+ y/y CIS growth. The AI inference/CIS pipeline remains 'exceptionally strong' with 8-9 figure ARR deals in the mix. Low-teens CY27 growth based on already-signed deals only; new large deals would be upside.

bullets.title: SNAP: SPECS AR headset launches Wednesday at $2,195; KeyBanc Sector Weight, ecosystem key watchpoint
bullets.body: KeyBanc maintains Sector Weight on SNAP ahead of SPECS launching Wednesday (Sept 16) as a full spatial AR headset with 3D display priced at $2,195. Meaningful volume not expected in year one; developer ecosystem and launch app availability are the critical variables. Snap's Subscription business on track for $1.3B revenue in 2026 (+75% y/y, >$900M EBITDA); SPECS estimated to lose $200M-$400M annually.

bullets.title: RBLX: Roth raises PT to $60 from $55 on structural improvements and pre-roll ad monetization
bullets.body: Roth increased its Roblox price target to $60 (from $55), citing confidence in the platform's structural transformation. Discovery and engagement feature improvements are driving growth, and pre-roll ad monetization is in testing. Developer Conference feedback reinforced support for the platform's directional shift. RBLX was down 2.6% pre-market.

bullets.title: Hedgeye Risk Ranges: Bullish MSFT, AAPL, META, SNOW; Bearish AMZN, GOOGL, TSLA; NVDA Neutral
bullets.body: Hedgeye's 9/15 Risk Range signals show MSFT (buy 485/sell 513), AAPL (buy 318/sell 340), META (buy 602/sell 682), and SNOW (buy 311/sell 357) in bullish trend; AMZN, GOOGL, and TSLA in bearish trend. NVDA is neutral. VIX flipped from Neutral to Bullish. Hedgeye separately flags long software (IGV, NOW) and bearish AVGO amid South Korean KOSPI semiconductor de-rating signals.

bullets.title: NVDA commits $1.5B to SoftBank SB Energy IPO; $50B valuation, $439B backlog
bullets.body: NVIDIA has contractually committed to purchase $1.5B of non-voting equity in SB Energy (proposed Nasdaq IPO: 'SBE') via private placement at IPO price. SoftBank targets a $50B valuation; SB Energy operates 8.8 GW-IT of signed data center capacity with ~$439B backlog. The company is 6M26 revenue of $138.7M (+67% y/y) but posting significant operating losses. OpenAI is also a strategic investor.

bullets.title: GLW: Mizuho cuts PT to $180 from $210 on lower SOX multiple; Springboard FCF growth lags sales
bullets.body: Mizuho reduced its Corning price target to $180 from $210, citing a lower SOX index multiple. Corning entered a $2B equity distribution agreement; the Springboard plan includes FCF growth that trails sales and earnings growth due to asset-heavy furnace capex commitments.

bullets.title: RDNT: Hedgeye moves to Active Long with $96 PT (30% upside); 2027 EBITDA 19% above Street
bullets.body: Hedgeye initiated RDNT as an Active Long at a $96 price target (17x 2027E EV/EBITDA, 30% upside). Their 2027 Adj. EBITDA forecast of $500M is 19% above Street consensus of $421M. PET/CT volumes have doubled to 29,000/quarter, revenue per scan ~$2,050 vs. blended average $184, and SmartMammo AI generates $40 cash-pay per mammogram with 40-45% East Coast adoption improving cancer detection by 21%.

bullets.title: DKNG: Gaming de-rated 18% YTD; JPM flags FY26 EBITDA guidance $700-900M as questioned, estimates $713M
bullets.body: JPM's gaming & lodging sector note flags digital gaming stocks (DKNG -38%, RSI -16%) as the most pressured segment in a sector that has de-rated 18% YTD (-2.6x EV/EBITDA). Regulatory clarity is not expected until mid-2027. JPM estimates FY26 EBITDA of $713M vs. the company's guided range of $700-900M, which analysts are questioning.

bullets.title: AFRM: GS highlights BNPL on strong secular growth and favorable credit at Communacopia; Truist warns PCE decelerating 150-200bps
bullets.body: Goldman Sachs highlighted AFRM and BNPL names at the Communacopia conference citing strong secular growth and favorable credit conditions. Truist separately warns that PCE growth will decelerate 150-200bps over the next 12-18 months as the savings rate falls near 3% and spending has outpaced income — though they note deceleration is 'largely priced in' to payment stocks.

bullets.title: TSLA: Musk flags Tesla-SpaceX R&D fab in Austin; open to combination; chip supply cited as AI scaling bottleneck
bullets.body: Elon Musk on the All-In podcast flagged Tesla and SpaceX are building a joint R&D semiconductor fab in Austin to secure chip supply, citing Taiwan dependence as an AI scaling risk. Musk left open the possibility of a Tesla-SpaceX combination given extensive collaboration. Hedgeye has TSLA in bearish trend (buy 346/sell 378).
